lens: Is the inference sound as statistics? Multiple comparisons; effect size and interval with every estimate; group construction read in the code; group independence and shared members; n after filtering; post-hoc or unprinted thresholds; the reference distribution a module score is read against; and whether the design would have produced a null.
what_i_read: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py (statistics helpers L336-395; _classify_sample L1599-1619; COMPARATOR_BUCKETS/FET_COMPARATOR_BUCKETS L295-329; derive_part_b L1946-2330; collect_part_c L2368-2446; derive_part_c L2447-2600; collect_part_d L2602-2783; derive_part_d L2784-2940)
research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json (part_b per_platform + pooled contrasts; part_c per_gene/coordination/group labels; part_d correlations/specificity/mechanism_tests/fet_signature)
git log -S over emc_atr_vulnerability.py for every numeric cut-off
central_claim: On public data the FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis is only weakly supported for EMC: EMC tumours' DDR transcripts are elevated no more than their generic proliferation (part B, GENERIC_ONLY / tier WEAK), the CRISPR knockout readout is saturated and cannot discriminate even against a matched sarcoma comparator (part C), and of four pre-registered mechanism tests on ATR-inhibitor sensitivity exactly one passes and it is a statement about the drug rather than about EMC (part D).

p1s.summary: The one mechanism test the paper reports as PASSING clears its proliferation bar by rho 0.0155 - 0.41x the standard error the paper itself computes - and the bar is an undisclosed 1.15x multiplier applied across two different measurement scales and two different line sets. The paper applies interval reasoning to three other rho comparisons in the same section and not to this one.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py derive_part_d: `srec["beats_the_proliferation_control"] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)`. Artifact emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity: dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = 0.2123; proliferation_control_rho = -0.1711. Bar = 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.19677; margin = 0.01553. The paper's own SI-grade statement (section 5): "At n ~ 700 the standard error on a single rho is ~ 0.038" (verified: 1/sqrt(697) = 0.0379). The two rho are not measured on the same lines or the same scale: the dependency rho is n=597 (azd6738) / n=565 (ve-822) CRISPR-and-drug lines, the proliferation rho is n=704 / n=711 expression-and-drug lines (artifact correlations block). The module states the scale problem in a comment - "a dependency predictor is on a different scale and sign from an expression predictor ... only meaningful as 'is this bigger than growth rate'" - and section 5's table renders it as a bare tick, "vs proliferation control (rho = -0.171) | checkmark beats it". Neither the 1.15x factor, the margin, the differing n, nor the scale caveat is printed.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print the bar as it is coded (|rho| > 1.15 x |rho_proliferation| = 0.197), print the margin (0.212 vs 0.197), and extend the section's own interval sentence to this row: at SE ~ 0.04 the passing predictor is not separable from the proliferation control either. Removing or weakening the existing 'no interval is computed anywhere' paragraph would re-break it.

p1s.summary: Part C's 'properly matched fusion-negative sarcoma comparator' shares members with the exposure class: its own subtype list contains Ewing Sarcoma, and the sibling artifact records ten sarcoma lines that are FET by disease label but not by the caller. The paper says the old comparator's limitation 'is now removed'.
p1s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.matched_comparator_subtype_labels contains 'Ewing Sarcoma' (alongside Chordoma, Leiomyosarcoma, Synovial Sarcoma, ...). The FET group is contaminated in the opposite direction: fet_lines_subtype_labels = ['Clear Cell Sarcoma','Ewing Sarcoma','Osteosarcoma','Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma/MFH/High-Grade Spindle Cell Sarcoma'] - osteosarcoma and UPS are not FET-driven diseases. fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> fet_grouping_by_fusion_call.agreement_with_label_grouping = {'n_label_only': 10, 'n_call_only': 37, 'n_both': 18}, with grouping.FET_rearranged.Ewing.n_with_crispr = 27 and grouping.n_FET_lines_total = 28 by label against 55 by call; that artifact's own _caveat says to 'use the disagreement between the two as the uncertainty, not either alone'. The producing module carries the bias note (_comparator_caveat, 'a caller miss puts a FET-positive line in the comparator'); the manuscript carries neither the note nor the count, and section 4 states 'That limitation is now removed'. Direction: contamination biases toward the null, which is the reported result, so the verdict INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND is not overturned - the overclaim is 'removed'.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace 'that limitation is now removed' with the two disagreement counts (10 label-only, 37 call-only, 18 both) and name Ewing Sarcoma as present in the comparator, stating that the contamination runs toward the null the section reports. Dropping the counts again would re-break it.

p1s.summary: Part B's 'elevated' cut of 0.2 is read against no reference distribution, and the artifact already contains an empirical one that reaches 1.7x the cut. On the verdict-carrying platform, two COMPARATOR groups that contain no EMC differ by more than any DDR concept does.
p1s.evidence: Recomputed from emc-atr-vulnerability.json per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].scores using the same Welch as the module (GIST n=3 vs DFSP n=3, no EMC in either arm): control_oxphos delta +0.334 (t 4.97), proliferation_mitotic -0.089 (t -3.63), ATR_CHK1_activity -0.173 (t -2.29), control_adipogenesis +0.098 (t 2.69). The three DDR concepts the paper counts as clearing the cut are +0.245, +0.311, +0.256. So an arbitrary sarcoma-pair contrast on this platform reaches 0.334, above the 0.2 cut and above every DDR term. This matters for WHICH negative is reported, not whether it is negative: `signature_present = bool(ddr_up_raw)` is what selects GENERIC_ONLY (tier WEAK) over the stronger NO_DDR_SIGNATURE_IN_EMC_TUMOURS verdict (emc_atr_vulnerability.py L2322-2330). The paper states the underpowering honestly - 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours and no minimum detectable effect was computed' - but never takes the free empirical null sitting in its own scores block.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add the comparator-vs-comparator contrast as the empirical null beside the 0.2 cut (GIST vs DFSP: oxphos +0.334, t 4.97) and say that raw elevation of three DDR concepts at +0.245 to +0.311 sits inside it, so the WEAK tier's 'signature_present = yes' predicate is a threshold crossing rather than a measured signal. Deleting the 'no minimum detectable effect was computed' sentence would make it worse.

p1s.summary: An undisclosed design confound in the verdict-carrying contrast: on GPL3290 the EMC and DFSP samples were hybridised against a CRH reference and the GIST samples against UHR (Universal Human Reference), so group and reference channel are partly collinear in a two-colour log-ratio readout. The paper says 'on the same print run', which is true of the array and not of the reference.
p1s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290...'].sample_annotations_verbatim: the 10 EMC rows read 'STT3699-Myxoid Chondrosarcoma | CRH-mRNA | ...', the 3 DFSP rows 'STT3126-DFSP | CRH | ...', the 3 GIST rows 'STT2001c-GIST-Total RNA-WT | UHR | ...'. The same block records value_kind = 'two-colour log-ratio vs a reference pool (RELATIVE)'. Per-sample z-scoring against each sample's own background removes scale but not the reference's gene-wise composition. Recomputed with the reference held constant (EMC n=10 vs DFSP n=3, both CRH): ATR-CHK1 +0.158 (t 2.74), S-phase/E2F +0.281 (t 3.81), DNA-damage checkpoint +0.250 (t 3.41), MYC targets +0.376 (t 5.20), oxphos +0.551 (t 8.04), adipogenesis +0.267 (t 6.66). The qualitative reading - DDR concepts move, non-DDR controls move as much or more - is unchanged, so this is a disclosure defect rather than a refutation.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State in section 3.4 that half the six-sample comparator was hybridised against a different reference RNA than the EMC arm, and give the reference-matched EMC-vs-DFSP contrast as the check that the reading survives. Leaving 'on the same print run' as the only design statement re-breaks it.

p2s.summary: Rows that fall into no group: 7 of GSE24369's 42 samples are `unclassified` and invisible to every printed summary. Five are solitary fibrous tumours - tumour biopsies of exactly the comparator class - and COMPARATOR_BUCKETS has no pattern for them; two are skeletal-muscle pooled RNA that miss `normal_or_reference` (which matches only 'normal'/'reference'/'universal') and are excluded only by accident. Across all eleven platforms read, 77 samples are unclassified.
p2s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py derive_part_b: `comp_idx = [i for k, v in groups.items() if k not in ("EMC", "unclassified", "normal_or_reference") for i in v]` - unclassified rows enter neither arm. Artifact class_counts for GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz: {'EMC': 6, 'LGFMS': 17, 'desmoid_fibromatosis': 6, 'fibrosarcoma': 6, 'unclassified': 7}; the seven verbatim annotations are GSM600963-600967 'Solitary fibrous tumor 1..5 | soft tissue | sample type: tumor biopsy' and GSM600968/600969 'Skeletal muscle pooled RNA 1..2'. class_counts_across_all_platforms: unclassified 77. NOT load-bearing, recomputed: adding the 5 solitary fibrous tumours to the 29-line comparator leaves every DDR concept at |delta| <= 0.054 with |t| <= 0.9 (ATM -0.000, ATR-CHK1 +0.022, replication stress -0.004, stalled fork -0.003, S-phase +0.053, checkpoint +0.053) and the non-DDR sets still the only movers (MYC +0.098 t 3.87, oxphos +0.123 t 6.70). The verdict-carrying platform GPL3290 has ZERO unclassified rows.

p2s.summary: Section 4's 'fraction dependent' column is panel-wide over 1,178 CRISPR lines of every lineage, not the 91-line sarcoma pool the sentence and the table describe, and no n is printed for it anywhere.
p2s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py derive_part_c: `"frac_dependent_panel_wide": round(sum(1 for v in vals[g].values() if v < DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD) / max(1, len(vals[g])), 3)` - `vals[g]` is every model with CRISPR data (part_c.n_models_with_crispr = 1178). The paper prints these values inside a sentence reading 'the axis sits at the floor in both groups - mean -1.340 across the sarcoma pool, 99.2-100 % of lines dependent on ATR and CHEK1'. Recomputed over the 91-line sarcoma pool from part_c.gene_effect_by_line and part_c.groups: ATR 1.000 (paper 0.992), ATRIP 0.769 (paper 0.726), CHEK1 1.000, WEE1 1.000, RPL5 1.000, ATM 0.000 (paper 0.007). No conclusion moves; the n attached to the number is wrong.

p2s.summary: Not every cut-off the paper applies is printed, contrary to section 1's own promise ('The cuts themselves, stated so they can be checked - the reporting half of the promise above, which was not being kept').
p2s.evidence: Printed: delta > 0.2, gene effect < -0.5, |rho| >= 0.15, and `signature_specific_to_DDR`. Not printed anywhere in the manuscript: `atri_specific` = |rho_ATRi| > 0.1 AND |rho_ATRi| > 1.5 x |rho_controls| (derive_part_d); `beats_the_proliferation_control` = |rho| > 1.15 x |rho_proliferation|; a concept is skipped unless >= 8 of its genes match the platform (`if len(genes) < 8: continue`, derive_part_b); a correlation is skipped unless >= 15 lines are common (`if len(common) < 15`); MIN_GROUP_N = 5; MIN_SCORED_CONCEPTS = 3; and the blindness rule's floor `sat["axis_mean_sarcoma_pool"] < -1.0`.

p2s.summary: The DDR-specificity predicate compares proliferation-ADJUSTED DDR sets against RAW controls, and section 3.4's table prints an em-dash in the adjusted column for every control row - withholding the fact that oxidative phosphorylation is the only set of any kind still above the 0.2 cut after adjustment. The withheld number supports the paper's own reading.
p2s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py L2307-2322: `ddr_up_adj` is read from `adj` (proliferation-adjusted) while `ctrl_up` is read from `raw`, and `signature_specific_to_DDR = bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1`. The adjusted control values exist - `adj = _pool("contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma_PROLIFERATION_ADJUSTED", tested + ctrls)` - and the artifact's pooled_proliferation_adjusted_contrast gives control_oxphos +0.2014 (t 2.49), control_adipogenesis +0.0353 (t 1.02), control_generic_DNA_repair -0.0052, control_myogenesis -0.0374, against every DDR concept at <= +0.128. Recomputed: making the predicate symmetric (controls also adjusted) gives ctrl_up = ['control_oxphos'], len 1 <= 1, and the verdict is unchanged because ddr_up_adj is empty either way. So the asymmetry is real and not outcome-determining; the em-dash is a reporting loss.

p2s.summary: The held-out FET signature's negative training class silently contains FET-called lines: `fet_ids` is the CRISPR-intersected FET set (55) while 81 models carry a FET call, so up to 26 FET-positive models without CRISPR data are trained as non-FET.
p2s.evidence: collect_part_d: `fet_ids = set((part_c_inputs or {}).get("groups", {}).get("FET_any_lineage") or [])`, and collect_part_c builds that group as `sorted(fet_ids & have)` where `have = set(ge.index)` is the CRISPR index. part_c.n_models_with_a_FET_fusion_call = 81 against group_sizes.FET_any_lineage = 55. `train_neg = sorted((have - fet_ids) - drug_lines)` = 928 lines. Bound: at most 26 of 928 (2.8 %). Direction: dilutes the signature toward the null, and the test is reported as failing (rho -0.138), so no conclusion moves.

p2s.summary: No multiple-comparison correction is stated or applied anywhere, and the number of tests actually run is never stated.
p2s.evidence: grep -niE 'bonferroni|benjamini|false discovery|fdr|multiple compar|multiple test|p-value' over the manuscript and emc_atr_vulnerability.py returns one hit, a code comment explaining that p-values are deliberately not computed ('report the statistic and n, never a p-value that cannot be computed exactly', L340). Tests actually computed: part D is 7 drugs x 10 predictors = 70 Spearman correlations, all present in artifact part_d...correlations; part B is 12 concepts x 4 contrast families across 11 scored platforms. The paper prints 4 predictor rows and 7 drug rows of the 70. Genuine mitigants that should be said rather than left implicit: part D's four mechanism tests carry pre-registered directions (`_prediction_directions`), and part B's cut is explicitly 'with no significance requirement', so its t values are descriptive. But 'of four pre-registered mechanism tests, one passes' is a selection from 70 computed correlations and the denominator is never given.

p2s.summary: Gene-set n after filtering is never stated; the overlap arithmetic in section 3.4 uses nominal set sizes, not the members that actually scored on the platform.
p2s.evidence: Artifact per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290...'].n_geneset_genes_matched: ATM_signalling 39 of the 61 the paper names, ATR_CHK1 35 of 37, replication_stress 35 of 48, stalled_fork 17 of 19, S_phase_E2F 182 of 200, DNA_damage_checkpoint 181 of 200, MYC 179 of 200, mitotic 185 of 199, controls 170-177 of 200. Section 3.2 prints the nominal sizes and section 3.4 prints '12 / 12 concepts scored' but never the matched counts. Section 3.4's overlap figures are computed on nominal sizes; recomputed from emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#gene_sets.concepts they are exactly right as stated (9/37 = 24.3 %, 54/200 = 27.0 %, 68/200 = 34.0 %, unrelated controls 2.0-6.5 %, non-clearing DDR 3.3-15.8 %) - so the arithmetic is sound, the scope label is the gap.

p2s.summary: Section 5's headline n is not the analysis n for any statistic in the section.
p2s.evidence: The setup sentence gives '956 lines with ceralasertib/AZD6738 and 892 with berzosertib/VE-822'; those are artifact n_lines_with_residual. Every correlation in the section is computed on the intersection with a predictor: n = 597 / 565 for the dependency predictor and n = 704 / 711 for every expression predictor. The per-drug table does print its own n, so the defect is confined to the setup sentence.

_verdict_note: supported_with_reservations / minor_revision. No blocker. Every defect I found runs toward the null the paper already reports, and the two I could test by recomputation (the excluded solitary-fibrous rows on GSE24369; the mixed reference channel on GPL3290) leave the qualitative reading unchanged. WHAT CAME BACK SOUND, checked rather than assumed: (1) every printed number in sections 3.4, 4 and 5 re-derives from the committed artifact - I recomputed GSE24369's twelve contrasts from `scores` with an independent Welch and got the paper's values to the last digit (ATM -0.004, ATR-CHK1 +0.011, replication stress -0.000, stalled fork -0.009, S-phase +0.044, checkpoint +0.045, MYC t 3.34, oxphos t 5.92, adipogenesis +0.047 t 2.11), and the seven-drug table matches `correlations` exactly (azd6738 +0.252 t 6.35 n 597; ve-822 +0.173 t 4.16 n 565; mk-1775 +0.157 t 3.89 n 601; olaparib +0.034 n 601; talazoparib -0.053 n 595; bortezomib +0.021 n 596; paclitaxel +0.007 n 597). (2) The unit of analysis is right: part B's t-tests are across SAMPLES, not genes - Welch df 12.1 for the 10-vs-6 contrast. (3) The verdict-carrying platform GPL3290 has ZERO unclassified rows; all 16 samples land in a group, so the invisible-row defect does not touch the series that carries the verdict. (4) The series-selection rule is coded, deterministic and prior (`_rank_key`: readable platforms, then EMC count), and GSE4303 wins on 10 vs 6 EMC exactly as the paper says. (5) 'Fixed before the numbers' is verifiable and holds: `git log -S` for 0.2, -0.5, 0.15, 1.15 and 1.5 * abs(c0) over emc_atr_vulnerability.py each return the single commit 922366a42, the file's first of eight - so no cut-off, including the two undisclosed multipliers, has moved since it was written. (6) The passing test is NOT a CRISPR-screen-scale artifact - I ran the negative control the paper does not: pan-essential RPL5 and PLK1 gene effect against the same drug residuals give rho +0.037 / -0.011 (azd6738) and +0.036 / +0.026 (ve-822), and near-neutral ATM gives +0.045 / +0.045, against +0.252 / +0.173 for the ATR axis. A globally shifted Chronos profile does not manufacture the correlation. (7) The hold-out is genuinely non-circular: `train_pos`/`train_neg` both subtract `drug_lines`. (8) Part C has no orphan row - every sarcoma line with CRISPR sits in exactly one of FET_sarcoma_only (20) and matched_sarcoma_FET_negative (71). (9) The coordination analysis uses the comparator's own bottom-quartile fraction as the null instead of 0.25^3, and says why. (10) Section 5's 'a mean over TWO drugs, not three' is exactly right: drugs_named_but_absent_from_this_release.non_DDR_controls = ['doxorubicin'], n_drugs.non_DDR_controls = 2. (11) Section 1's code citations are correct: DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5 is depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py line 97, imported at emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 76, and the 0.2 cuts plus `signature_specific_to_DDR` sit at emc_atr_vulnerability.py 2309-2322. (12) The per-line GDSC residual is implemented as described - median across every drug for that line, subtracted.
